card.summary: S. 1462, the Fix Our Forests Act, aims to improve forest management activities on National Forest System land, public land under the Bureau of Land Management, and Tribal land to reduce wildfire risks and return resilience to overgrown, fire-prone areas. The bill establishes programs, interagency centers, and streamlined procedures for hazardous fuels reduction, prescribed burning, reforestation, community protection, litigation reforms, and disaster assistance for wildland firefighters.

summary: The Disaster Assistance Simplification Act directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to create a single, unified intake process and system for people, businesses, and organizations applying for federal disaster assistance. The system aims to consolidate applications across multiple disaster assistance programs, allow applicants to check application statuses and update information, distribute recovery resources, and enable direct communication between agencies and survivors while meeting data security and privacy requirements.

affected_groups.effect: Can use a consolidated application system to apply for disaster assistance, check status updates, update recovery information, and communicate directly with disaster assistance agencies.
Responsible for developing, establishing, and managing the unified intake process, certifying disaster assistance agencies, and submitting implementation reports and briefings to Congress.

Collaborate with FEMA, share disaster assistance information under specified rules, update application questions upon request, and assume liability for any unauthorized disclosures caused by their personnel.

key_provisions: Requires FEMA to develop and establish a unified intake process and system for disaster assistance applicants within 360 days of enactment.
Allows a consolidated application for various forms of federal disaster assistance when appropriate.
Permits applicants to receive status updates, update their information throughout recovery, and receive information on additional recovery resources.
Grants the FEMA Administrator authority to waive the Paperwork Reduction Act for voluntary information collection related to a declared disaster.
Requires FEMA to meet specific data security standards, privacy impact assessments, and rules of behavior before collecting information into the unified application.
Mandates regular reports and congressional briefings from FEMA regarding implementation, as well as a report from the Government Accountability Office after three years.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or appropriations required to build and maintain the unified system.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Disaster Assistance Simplification Act directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to create a single, unified intake process and system for people, businesses, and organizations applying for federal disaster assistance. The system aims to consolidate applications across multiple disaster assistance programs, allow applicants to check application statuses and update information, distribute recovery resources, and enable direct communication between agencies and survivors while meeting data security and privacy requirements.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a government-wide administrative framework intended to connect multiple disaster assistance programs through a single intake system, potentially altering how federal agencies collect and share applicant data during declared emergencies.

title: Disaster Assistance Simplification Act
